text:
Incident Bot: ALERT — Elevated 5xx (504) and tail latency on /v1/generate in us-east-1. Canary rollout currently targeting 10% traffic to model-id: rdw-model-v2-q4. Auto-scaling AND fallback enabled. Paging oncall.

Kai (Oncall): on it. I’m collecting immediate metrics & checking canary vs stable split. :eyes:

Sam (Prod): customers A and B reported errors ~17:22 UTC. Their traffic is routed to canary. They're seeing timeout errors in logs. Important: both are enterprise contracts.

Emma (SRE): copying. Spinning up log grep and flame graphs. Can someone paste the canary routing config? I want to confirm headers.

Ravi (ML): that canary is v2-q4 (quantized int4 ABI). fallback route is configured to v1.2.3. We rolled 10% at 17:05 UTC. No other infra changes.

Lina (Eng): sharing quick traces. Looks like a spike in KV-cache misses + async queue backpressure for long-seq requests.

Lina (Eng): logs (redacted):
```
[17:23:11] worker-72 request_id=abc123 model=rdw-model-v2-q4 seq_len=2048 latency=3210ms outcome=timeout
[17:23:12] cache-miss key=prompt_prefix_42
[17:23:12] worker-72 retry attempt=1
[17:23:13] upstream 504
```

Emma (SRE): thanks. Hypothesis A: quantized kernel path regresses for long sequences causing stalls + downstream timeouts. Hypothesis B: autoscaler didn’t spin enough warm pods for canary traffic pattern (long-seq heavy). Need quick checks: 1) kernel errors on GPU logs 2) pod scale events 3) model version pin status.

Kai (Oncall): running checks now. Pod scaling history:
```
17:04 scale up +2 pods (pre-rollout)
17:20 no scale events
17:24 spike in pending queue
```

Ravi (ML): quick diff between canary and stable perf (tail p95):
```
v1.2.3 p95=480ms
v2-q4  p95=680ms (but p99 for long seq=2800ms)
```

Sam (Prod): is there customer-visible error rate? Ops dashboard: 2.3% error rate on canary traffic, overall infra error rate 0.4%.

Emma (SRE): can we temporarily route enterprise customers off canary? That buys time.

Lina (Eng): yes, we can pin routing by customer header. Command:
```
# remove enterprise header routing to canary
redwoodctl routing update --rule "customer in (CustA,CustB)" --route stable
```

Kai (Oncall): doing that now. Update: CustA/CustB pinned to stable at 17:32 UTC. Errors dropped for those customers.

Ravi (ML): since p99 long-seq is high, I'm inclined to pause rollout and pin global traffic back to v1.2.3 for now. We should not roll forward while hypothesis unresolved.

Emma (SRE): agree. Two mitigations: 1) roll back canary to v1.2.3 (global) OR 2) disable q4 kernel path for long-seq requests (patch). Rollback is faster.

Lina (Eng): risk assessment: rollback will restore prior performance but we lose canary telemetry. Patch might be safer long-term but takes 30-60m.

Kai (Oncall): what's model pin status? Running check:
```
$ redwoodctl models describe rdw-model --env canary
active_version: v2-q4
pinned_versions:
 - global: none
 - customer: CustA->v1.2.3, CustB->v1.2.3
```

Ravi (ML): suggestion: pin canary pool to v1.2.3 and halt further rollout. Also add a small rollout test with long-seq prompts in staging.

Sam (Prod): customers are stable after pin. 👍

Lina (Eng): Initiating rollback now. @Deploy Bot can you start rollback to v1.2.3 for canary pool and mark rollout paused?

Deploy Bot: acknowledged — initiating rollback for rdw-model-v2-q4 -> v1.2.3 on canary pool.

Deploy Bot: update: 6/6 canary instances switched to v1.2.3. Health checks passing. Canary traffic now served by v1.2.3.

Emma (SRE): monitoring metrics. p99 tail dropped back to expected range. No more 504s in the last 4 minutes.

Ravi (ML): logging note: we captured kernel traces from one failing instance, will upload to S3 and attach to RCA ticket.

Lina (Eng): adding short timeline summary for RCA:
- 17:05 UTC: v2-q4 canary 10% rollout
- 17:20 UTC: gradual increase in long-seq requests -> KV-cache miss spike
- 17:22–17:28 UTC: p99 latency climbs; enterprise customers hit 504s
- 17:32 UTC: enterprise customers pinned to stable
- 17:35 UTC: rollback of canary to v1.2.3 completed
- 17:40 UTC: errors returned to baseline

Kai (Oncall): immediate mitigation complete. Handoff plan: we'll create a follow-up RCA doc with diffs, logs, and testcases. @Ravi can you own ML hypothesis and kernel-level investigation? @Emma own infra scaling checks and runbook updates. @Lina write up timeline and attach logs.

Ravi (ML): I’ll own kernel/quantization hypothesis. Next steps: reproduce with longer sequence in internal harness, compare q4 vs q8 and ORT paths.

Emma (SRE): I’ll add autoscale thresholds to avoid warm-pool starvation for long-seq traffic and add a canary gating check for p99_long_seq before rollouts.

Lina (Eng): I'll open ticket RDW-INC-517 with attachments, link to dashboard and S3 logs, and schedule RCA sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Also note: do not restart canary rollout until we have reproduction.

Sam (Prod): communicating to customers that issue mitigated and rollback in place. Will send follow-up update once RCA is ready.

Kai (Oncall): closing incident channel for active pages. Leaving thread open for RCA discussion. Good job team. :clap:
